sets.title: PSM III Expert Essay & Situational Practice Assessment Set 1
sets.description: Full-length 24-essay prompt PSM III exam simulation. 150 minutes (2.5 hours) time limit. Features interactive AI & Rubric Evaluator with model answer benchmarks and domain recommendations.

questions.prompt: [Prompt 1] [Empiricism & Transparency] Explain how a Scrum Master establishes transparency when a Scrum Team is working in an environment with high technical complexity, shifting stakeholder demands, and unquantified legacy technical debt. What concrete steps would you take, and how do you inspect and adapt? (Set 1 Context Variation)

rubricCriteria.name: Empirical Pillars
rubricCriteria.description: Explicitly references Transparency, Inspection, and Adaptation as interconnected feedback loops.

rubricCriteria.name: Artifact Integrity
rubricCriteria.description: Leverages Product Backlog and Definition of Done to make technical debt visible.

rubricCriteria.name: Coaching Action
rubricCriteria.description: Coaches team and leadership toward empirical decision making instead of predictive management.

questions.modelAnswer: To establish transparency in a complex, legacy-burdened environment, I start by coaching the team to make all work—including technical debt, refactoring, and technical spikes—explicit in the Product Backlog and governed by a rigorous Definition of Done. First, we make technical debt transparent by making its impact visible to the Product Owner and stakeholders through empirical metrics such as Sprint cycle time, defect rates, and Increment stability. Second, I facilitate the Inspection of this debt during Sprint Planning and Sprint Retrospectives, helping the Developers negotiate technical debt remediation items into Sprint Backlogs linked directly to Sprint Goals. Third, Adaptation occurs as the Scrum Team refines the Definition of Done over time to raise the quality bar, ensuring no new debt is introduced.

recommendation.action: Study how to make technical debt, unquantified risks, and complex dependencies transparent via Increments.

questions.prompt: [Prompt 2] [Coaching Stance & Servant Leadership] You enter an organization where management treats the Scrum Master as a junior administrative coordinator who schedules meetings and takes notes. How do you shift the organization's mindset to recognize the Scrum Master as a true servant leader accountable for Scrum Team effectiveness? (Set 1 Context Variation)

rubricCriteria.name: Accountability Clarity
rubricCriteria.description: Articulates SM accountability for Scrum Team effectiveness and organizational enablement.

rubricCriteria.name: Organizational Coaching Strategy
rubricCriteria.description: Outlines a structured strategy to educate leadership, POs, and teams on servant leadership.

rubricCriteria.name: Impediment Removal Focus
rubricCriteria.description: Transitions from administrative tasks to high-impact organizational impediment removal.

questions.modelAnswer: I address this fundamental misunderstanding by combining education, modeling servant leadership, and delivering visible organizational value. 1. Education & Framing: I organize workshops for leadership and stakeholders referencing the 2020 Scrum Guide, clarifying that the Scrum Master is accountable for the Scrum Team's effectiveness and for leading, training, and coaching the organization in its Scrum adoption. 2. Facilitation vs. Administration: I coach the Developers to self-manage their event logistics, freeing my capacity to focus on removing systemic organizational impediments. 3. Demonstrating Impact: I target high-friction organizational blockers—such as cross-departmental dependencies—and systematically resolve them.

recommendation.topic: Enterprise Servant Leadership & Agile Coaching Stance
recommendation.action: Refine your executive coaching stance, shifting organizations away from command-and-control to servant leadership.
